patterns.usage_note: Emphatic にして takes a measure of time, an age, or an ordinal attempt and presents it as remarkable — startlingly short (一夜にして), startlingly late or early (三十路にして, 五十歳にして), or hard-won (三度目にして). It carries a formal, written flavour and survives in set phrases such as ローマは一日にして成らず; casual speech would use で or たった〜で instead. The same form has two other lives worth recognizing: joining two properties of one person (学者にして詩人), and, chiefly in older or stiff prose, meaning "even" (彼にしてこの失敗) where modern Japanese would say 彼でさえ or 彼ほどの人でも.

examples.ruby: 長年[ながねん]の努力[どりょく]が、一夜[いちや]にして水[みず]の泡[あわ]となった。
examples.english: Years of effort came to nothing in the space of a single night.

examples.ruby: 三十路[みそじ]にして、彼女[かのじょ]は初[はじ]めて筆[ふで]を執[と]った。
examples.english: It was in her thirties that she first took up the pen.

examples.ruby: 三度目[さんどめ]の挑戦[ちょうせん]にして、彼[かれ]の小説[しょうせつ]は賞[しょう]を取[と]った。
examples.english: On his third try, and only then, his novel took the prize.
